question: If the curved surface area of a cylinder of height 6 cm is 264 cm² , then its volume is: (Use pi=22/7 )
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Radius (r) = Curved Surface Area ÷ (2 × π × h)

⇒ r = 264 ÷ (2 × 22/7 × 6) = 264 ÷ (264/7) = 7 cm

Volume of a cylinder is directly proportional to its CSA: Volume = ½ × CSA × r

⇒ Volume = ½ × 264 × 7 = 132 × 7 = 924 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 924 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 264 cm²

Height (h) = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of a cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

Volume of a cylinder = π × r² × h

 
 
 
 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• h = 6 cm 
• r = ? 
• CSA = 264 cm² 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × π × r × h = 264

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × 6 = 264

⇒ (264/7) × r = 264

⇒ r = 7 cm

Now, substitute the value of radius to calculate the volume:

⇒ Volume = π × r² × h

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (7)² × 6

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 49 × 6

⇒ Volume = 22 × 7 × 6

⇒ Volume = 154 × 6 = 924 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 924 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

TSA = 2 × π × r × (r + h), where 'r' is the base radius and 'h' is the height.

Volume of a Cone

Volume = (1/3) × π × r² × h, which is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder having the same dimensions.

Hollow Cylinder Volume

Volume = π × h × (R² − r²), where 'R' is the outer radius and 'r' is the inner radius.
